headline: Stocks rebound into Friday, but hot inflation and an AI-debt scare keep rate fears alive
summary: The S&P 500 rose 0.3% on Thursday and ended a three-day slide. Money rotated out of AI and chip names into health care, financials and retailers. Futures are slightly higher this morning, but the index is on pace for a losing week after September CPI came in at 3.7% and wholesale prices jumped 1.3%. With Fed Chair Warsh declining to signal the next move, today's positioning favors areas with earnings support and pricing power over the AI hardware names that are still unwinding.

fed.note: Warsh declined Friday to signal October or December moves. A hold is the base case; a December hike is priced as likely.

drivers.title: Inflation re-accelerates on energy
drivers.body: September CPI rose 0.6% on the month and 3.7% from a year earlier, with gasoline up 9.1%. Producer prices then jumped 1.3% against a 0.5% forecast. Core CPI ran at 2.6% annually, so the pressure is concentrated in fuel but is spreading to shelter and used cars.

drivers.title: Fed holds back guidance, hike risk shifts to December
drivers.body: Warsh said in Bangkok that he will not prejudge the October or December meetings. Odds of an Oct 28 hike range from about 15% to 35% depending on the source. Prediction markets put a December hike near 79%. The Fed raised rates 25 bp in September.

drivers.title: AI-debt scare hits chips and data-center names
drivers.body: CoreWeave fell about 15% Wednesday on debt worries, and Dell dropped about 11% after a Barclays downgrade. Reuters-cited estimates put the combined loss in CoreWeave, Nebius, Oracle and Dell near $80 billion. CoreWeave bounced about 5% Thursday but was lower again premarket. ASML and Infineon fell 6–8% in Europe.

drivers.title: Rotation lifts breadth and defensives
drivers.body: Thursday's gain was broad. The equal-weight S&P rose 1.36% and the Russell 2000 gained 1.38%. Health care, financials and retail led, while Nvidia and AMD fell. Only 45% of S&P 500 stocks sit above their 50-day average, so this is a bounce within a weak trend.

drivers.title: Oil stays above $105 on Hormuz risk
drivers.body: Brent is set for a second weekly gain on attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz. The IEA will complete the remaining 100 million barrels of its March reserve release. Refiners and producers are the strongest part of the market. Fuel costs feed straight into the inflation data above.

drivers.title: Yields ease but stay near multi-year highs
drivers.body: The 10-year yield dipped below 5.04% Thursday on the hot PPI, then edged back above 5.08%. That is about 12 bp below mid-week. High-yield spreads tightened to 321 bp after a six-month high Wednesday. Real estate, homebuilders and small caps remain sensitive to any move back up.

drivers.title: Data is solid, which cuts both ways
drivers.body: September retail sales rose 0.8%, but only 0.2% excluding fuel. The Empire State survey jumped to 25.5, the highest since December 2021, while the Philadelphia Fed index fell to 20.9. Jobless claims were 199,000. Solid activity limits the case for a Fed pause.

risks.title: Hot inflation forces a hawkish Fed
risks.body: Another energy-driven inflation surprise could push December hike odds higher and send the 10-year yield back above 5.1%.

risks.title: AI-debt stress spreads
risks.body: CoreWeave's heavy debt and Dell's downgrade show how fragile AI financing is. Further credit stress could spread to the broader tech sector.

risks.title: Oil spike
risks.body: Further attacks near the Strait of Hormuz could push Brent higher, adding to inflation and hurting airlines and consumers.

risks.title: Earnings week concentration
risks.body: Netflix, GE, RTX, Meta, Tesla and IBM report next week, with Microsoft and Alphabet on Oct 28. Guidance will test current valuations.

risks.title: Thin gains under the surface
risks.body: With only 45% of S&P 500 stocks above their 50-day average, Thursday's rebound could fade quickly.

avoid.name: Homebuilders
avoid.detail: Homebuilding is the second-weakest industry with no stocks above their 200-day average, and the group is down 10–11% over three months.

avoid.name: Aerospace & defense
avoid.detail: The industry is near the bottom with 10% of stocks above their 200-day average, and ITA is down 10.2% over three months.

avoid.name: Airlines
avoid.detail: JETS is down 12.8% over three months with jet fuel costs high and Brent above $105.

avoid.name: Casinos and construction materials
avoid.detail: Both industries have no stocks above their 200-day average.

avoid.name: Oracle
avoid.detail: Down about 56% from its high and caught in the AI-debt selloff.

avoid.name: Solar
avoid.detail: TAN is down 20.7% over three months and 21.7% below its 200-day average.

sectors.name: Energy
sectors.note: The group is the strongest in the digest, with refiners at the top and 66% of stocks above their 200-day average. Brent above $105 and Hormuz risks support it. Refiners are stretched, so buy dips rather than chase.

sectors.name: Health Care
sectors.note: The sector was Thursday's best performer and 79% of stocks are above their 200-day average. Life sciences tools and managed care are the leaders. Falling yields and rotation out of AI help, and it works as a defensive area.

sectors.name: Consumer Staples
sectors.note: Beverages and tobacco lead, and the sector gained 3.7% over the past month. It is a defensive haven while AI names sell off and inflation stays high. Philip Morris reports Wednesday and Coca-Cola Oct 27.

sectors.name: Information Technology
sectors.note: Software and Microsoft are holding up while chips and hardware are being sold on AI-debt fears. Dell, Micron and Intel sit well below their highs. Favor software and platform names over hardware until the selling stabilizes.

sectors.name: Materials
sectors.note: Steel is the one strong pocket, but the sector overall is flat to lower over three months and construction materials are weak. Steel Dynamics reports Monday and Nucor the following week.

sectors.name: Communication Services
sectors.note: Meta is the one strong name and the sector is down 2.2% over the past month. Meta reports Wednesday after the close, so expect volatility into the event. Streaming and media are weak.

sectors.name: Utilities
sectors.note: Only 26% of stocks are above their 200-day average and the sector is down 5.7% over three months. Yields near 5.1% compete with its payouts, leaving little reason to overweight it.

sectors.name: Financials
sectors.note: Insurers and reinsurers are the strong pocket, while banks and brokers are weak and the sector is down 5.6% over three months. Travelers and M&T results this morning set the tone.

sectors.name: Real Estate
sectors.note: The weakest breadth in the digest, with 14% of stocks above their 50-day average and a 10.8% three-month decline. Yields near 5.1% weigh on it. Hotel REITs are the exception.

sectors.name: Industrials
sectors.note: Only 34% of stocks are above their 200-day average and aerospace, machinery and airlines are in downtrends. A few logistics and distribution names are strong. J.B. Hunt's margin miss and fuel costs are a drag. GE, RTX and Northrop report Tuesday.

sectors.name: Consumer Discretionary
sectors.note: Retailers rallied sharply Thursday, but homebuilders, auto parts, casinos and leisure are in clear downtrends. Pick specific retailers with strong charts rather than the whole sector.

picks.name: ExxonMobil
picks.thesis: Oil above $105 and a flow of money into energy support the trend. The setup weakens if Brent falls sharply on Hormuz de-escalation or the stock loses its 50-day average.

picks.name: Phillips 66
picks.thesis: Refiners are the sector's strongest industry and high crude prices are keeping margins in focus. A drop in refining margins or crude would undermine the case.

picks.name: West Pharmaceutical Services
picks.thesis: Health care is where money rotated Thursday and the stock is at its highs. A slide in the sector or falling short at earnings on Oct 29 would break the setup.

picks.name: Humana
picks.thesis: Managed care is among the strongest industries and 100% of the group is above its 200-day average. UnitedHealth's results also lifted the group. Policy or cost-trend surprises are the risk.

picks.name: Lilly (Eli)
picks.thesis: A defensive growth name that benefits from rotation out of tech. Earnings on Oct 29 are the next catalyst; a loss of the recent breakout area would invalidate the setup.

picks.name: Coca-Cola Company (The)
picks.thesis: Staples hold up when inflation and AI worries hit stocks. It is near its high and earnings come Oct 27. A rotation back into growth would reduce its appeal.

picks.name: Microsoft
picks.thesis: Software is outperforming hardware and Microsoft rose Thursday as chips fell. Earnings on Oct 28 are the test, and AI capex worries returning would hit it.

picks.name: MetLife
picks.thesis: Life insurers benefit from high yields and are among the stronger financials. Falling yields or credit stress would weaken the case.

picks.name: Reinsurance Group of America
picks.thesis: Reinsurers are a top industry with every stock above its 200-day average and the stock is at its high. A large catastrophe or reserve problem would invalidate it.

picks.name: Abercrombie & Fitch
picks.thesis: A retail leader that hit a 52-week high as retailers surged Thursday. Weak consumer data or a drop in retail would break the trend.

picks.name: Nucor
picks.thesis: Steel is the one strong group in a weak materials sector. The stock sits close to its 50-day average, so risk is tight; a break below it would invalidate the setup.

picks.name: Meta Platforms
picks.thesis: The only strong communication name, with analysts bullish. Earnings on Oct 21 are a big binary event, and an AI-spending scare could hit it.

picks.name: Park Hotels & Resorts
picks.thesis: Hotel REITs are the one strong real estate pocket. A rise in yields back above 5.1% or weaker travel demand would undermine it.

picks.name: Valero Energy
picks.thesis: The refining leader jumped on a Citi upgrade but is well above its 50-day average. Earnings on Oct 22 add event risk, so a pullback is the better entry.
